arguments.text: 8000 m, out-and-back legs of 1250 m. After the hard start, settle near critical power (pod about 160 W, boat about 104 W) and keep the reserve (w_bal_pod_frac) above about 40 pct until 1500 m to go; then spend it, final sprint (finish cue) at about 500 m to go. Calibration may be 10-25 pct off: check pod reserve vs boat reserve and paddler feel. Watch for drag changes (push_local drop, pod power up with GPS speed down) and radio messages.

arguments.message: Boat much slower than pod power predicts: drag, weed, or strong adverse current
Pod power over 112 pct of critical for 90 s

arguments.text: Good start. Settle into race rhythm now, smooth and long.

1.0 min: hard start, pod 206 W vs CP 161, pod reserve 76 pct. Cued ease to 158 s/500 over ground (leg 1 current helps about +0.17 m/s, so water pace about 167 = sustainable). Watches set: pod_reserve_low (<0.35), drag_jump (push_local < -0.35 for 20 s), over_cp_long.

arguments.reason: check paddler settled near critical power after the start

text: Set plan and watches; cued ease to 158 s/500 because the hard start was draining the reserve fast.

arguments.text: 2.8 min: settled. Pod 149 W (below pod CP 161), pod reserve 66 pct and steady; boat-model 108 W (above 104) and boat reserve 53 pct falling. Boat/pod power ratio now 0.72 vs 0.65 at calibration; push_local 0.30 vs push_along 0.18. Either the current is stronger than fitted (boat power overestimated) or the pod reads low. Check on leg 2 (return): if push_local goes strongly negative, it is current.

text: no cue: paddler settled near pod critical power at target pace; noted pod vs boat reserve divergence to check on the return leg.

arguments.text: You have plenty. Lift the effort a little and hold it.

5.8 min: pod 149 W vs pod CP 161 (sustainable 164), pod reserve 72 pct and rising; paddler says effort 2/10, plenty left. Boat reserve 38 pct and falling is likely wrong: push_local 0.27 > push_along 0.20, so the current is stronger than fitted and boat power is overestimated. Trusting pod + feel. Cued a modest push (no pace target, turn coming). Target pod about 160-165 W.

arguments.reason: check pod power after the push cue and the first turn; compare push_local on the return leg

text: Cued a modest push: pod power is below critical, pod reserve rising and the paddler reports 2/10; the falling boat reserve looks like an under-fitted current.

arguments.message: Pod power well below critical for 30 s: blow-up, problem, or easing

arguments.text: 7.9 min, leg 2 (south): push_local -0.10 vs push_along -0.15. On BOTH legs push_local sits about +0.06 above push_along, so it is not a current misfit: the boat sees about 11 pct more power than the pod relative to calibration (boat/pod ratio 0.72 vs 0.646). Boat reserve says 10 pct, empty in 115 m; pod says 67 pct, paddler at pod CP (162 W) after push cue. Test: if no blow-up by about 10-11 min, the boat CP is too low (about 116 W = 161 x 0.72); then correct cp_w with set_critical_power.

arguments.reason: confirm no blow-up despite boat reserve near empty; then correct boat critical power to about 116 W

text: no cue: paddler now at pod critical power after the push; boat-model reserve disagrees with pod on both legs, set a blow-up watch and a check in 3 min.

arguments.reason: Paddler held 108-116 W boat-model power for 7 min after a hard start with no fade and reports 5/10, plenty left; with boat CP 104 / 4.5 kJ the reserve would be empty. Pre-drift boat/pod ratio 0.72 x pod CP 161 = 116 W.

arguments.message: Speed through the water below 2.82 m/s for 40 s: fading, drag (weed), or easing

arguments.text: 8000 m, out-and-back legs of 1250 m. POD IS DRIFTING LOW since about 8 min (pod power fell 172 to 130 W while GPS speed held), so pod power, pod reserve and push_local are unreliable. Use boat-model power and speed through water; boat CP corrected to 115 W at 9.8 min. Hold speed through water about 3.05 m/s (boat about 110-115 W) to 1500 m to go, then build; finish cue at about 500 m to go. Ask the paddler how they feel every 10 min or so. Watch for drag (speed drop at same rate and feel) and radio messages.

9.8 min: pod drift. Pod fell 172 to 130 W from 7.4 to 9.8 min while GPS speed held 2.93 to 2.90 and rate 64; boat/pod ratio 0.72 to 0.85. Paddler now 5/10, plenty. Removed pod-based watches (pod_power_drop, pod_reserve_low, drag_jump); added speed_drop (speed_water < 2.82 for 40 s). Set boat cp_w 115 (1 of 3 used).

text: no cue: pod reading drifts low while boat speed holds; switched to boat-model power, corrected boat CP to 115 W, replaced pod-based watches with a speed-drop watch.

arguments.text: Looking strong. Lift a touch, long powerful strokes.

arguments.reason: after the turn onto leg 3 (north, current helps): check response to push, set a leg-matched pace target

arguments.text: 11.0 min: corrected boat model says 110 W vs CP 115, reserve 88 pct, sustainable water pace 161.7 vs 164.8 now. Cued a small push (no pace target, turn in 460 m). Aim boat power about 115-118 W.

text: Cued a small push: corrected boat model shows power below critical with 88 pct reserve and room to go 3 s/500 faster.
